findings.original_finding: The displayed block could read as equating both B′ >= 0 and the collateral inequality with B <= H(x). The latter alone does not rule out overpaying debt at an arbitrary sale, although the following first-crossing proof correctly retained the separate constraint.
findings.counterexample: For original debt B = 0 and any positive permitted sale, B <= H(x) can hold while B′ = -p(x)x is negative.
findings.correction_verified: Final display explicitly defines B′ and separately requires B′ >= 0; it states equivalence only for the collateral inequality. Read the revised display and the unchanged first-crossing proof; author record preserves the finding.

independent_review.bank: Recomputed the withdrawal source/use identity, sale face amount and equity, bridge-funded equity, senior bridge/depositor waterfall, asset-loss allocation, cancelled-share non-effect and public residual. Bad-recovery state does not reuse the full-repayment sale price. A larger bridge with retained extra cash does not create net worth.
independent_review.collateral: Independently expanded H(x), completed squares and checked global endpoint/vertex maxima and the first-crossing argument under strict positive prices, 0 < theta < 1, uniform-price receipts and nonnegative debt. Verified 400/9 partial sale, complete liquidation and impossible branches; exercise maximum 225/4 and minimum concession 31/4. Root brackets do not silently authorize negative debt.
independent_review.external: Separately reconstructed foreign currency receipts, principal and interest uses, private/official borrowing and reserve floor. Independently confirmed CA = FA = 51/2 H, opening NFA -36, valuation -18 and closing NFA -57/2. All current transactions occur after opening revaluation. National cash availability is a maintained consolidation assumption; financing availability is conditional. A quote change does not supply missing foreign currency.
independent_review.fiscal: Independently reconciled both dates, gross issuance versus stock change and the finite present-value test with opening cash available at date 1. Support of 15 acquires certain date-2 recovery 5 with date-1 value 50/11 and transfer 115/11; post-transfer surplus -71/11 plus stock-flow adjustment -16/11 produces B1 = 93. The full cash need is not reduced by classification, and the convention is explicitly not a universal bailout rule.
independent_review.uncertainty: Independently checked statewise minima, worst losses and worst regrets, then enumerated 401 exact severe-state probabilities. Expected-loss lower envelope has the stated 1/4 and 1/2 switches and ties; the A/B crossing at 3/8 is not optimal. Probability, social weights and feasible action set are supplied rather than inferred.
independent_review.solutions_and_instruction: Solved all numerical exercise components independently with Fractions and read every prompt against its solution. Exercise 7 supplies four distinct inference failures, concrete observations/design choices and evaluative criteria. Exercise 8 separates net currency exposure from maturity access. Retention answers and linked stress task agree.
independent_review.executable: Read all validation/calculation/CLI code and checker paths. Ran quiet check() with stdout/stderr capture and strict JSON serialization. Independently changed private FX borrowing to 8, bank recovery to 65 and terminal surplus to 100, obtaining official need 11/2, public recovery 0 and fiscal terminal -23/10. Separate new-quote 5/2 mutation leaves official F need unchanged and gives CA 85/4, valuation -9 and closing NFA -95/4.
